newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian AvtoVAZ shareholders vote on new issue.
newsitem.headline: Russian AvtoVAZ shareholders vote on new issue.

text.p: A meeting of shareholders of the Russian car manufacturer AvtoVAZ voted on Satuday to issue about 27 million new shares as part of a plan to restructure its debt to the government, Interfax news agency said.
Interfax said a package of 51 percent of shares plus one voting share would be transferred to the government in return for a 10-year extension of the deadline by which AvtoVAZ must pay off its debt.
The state will have the right to sell its stake as a whole or in parts if the plant defaulted on its debts for two months or more.
The plan to grant the extension was taken at a meeting of a special government commission headed by First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais earlier this month.

Faced with a gaping hole in the 1997 budget and battling with parliament over painful cuts in spending, the government has threatened to bankrupt companies which do not pay taxes or restructure their debt.

Under a government plan to restructure company debt, the companies must issue new equity comprising a controlling stake to be held as collateral by the state, or company debt that can also be held by the state.
AvtoVAZ is one of Russia's biggest debtors, with a debt to the government of 2.85 trillion roubles ($491.4 million).
